verses.zh: 希西家登基的时候年二十五岁，在耶路撒冷作王二十九年。他母亲名叫亚比雅，是撒迦利雅的女儿。
verses.en: Hezekiah was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem.[NOTE:1] His mother[NOTE:2] was Abijah,[NOTE:3] the daughter of Zechariah.
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
The parallel passage in 2 Kgs 18:2 has “Abi.”

verses.zh: 希西家行耶和华眼中看为正的事，效法他祖大卫一切所行的。
verses.en: He did what the Lord approved, just as his ancestor David had done.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “he did what was proper in the eyes of the Lord, according to all which David his father had done.”

verses.zh: 元年正月，开了耶和华殿的门，重新修理。
verses.en: In the first month of the first year of his reign, he opened the doors of the Lord’s temple and repaired them.

verses.zh: 他召众祭司和利未人来，聚集在东边的宽阔处，
verses.en: He brought in the priests and Levites and assembled them in the square on the east side.

verses.zh: 对他们说：「利未人哪，当听我说：现在你们要洁净自己，又洁净耶和华―你们列祖　神的殿，从圣所中除去污秽之物。
verses.en: He said to them: “Listen to me, you Levites! Now consecrate yourselves, so you can consecrate the temple of the Lord God of your ancestors.[NOTE:1] Remove from the sanctuary what is ceremonially unclean.

verses.zh: 我们列祖犯了罪，行耶和华―我们　神眼中看为恶的事，离弃他，转脸背向他的居所，
verses.en: For our fathers were unfaithful; they did what is evil in the sight of[NOTE:1] the Lord our God and abandoned him. They turned away[NOTE:2] from the Lord’s dwelling place and rejected him.[NOTE:3]

verses.zh: 封锁廊门，吹灭灯火，不在圣所中向以色列　神烧香，或献燔祭。
verses.en: They closed the doors of the temple porch and put out the lamps; they did not offer incense or burnt sacrifices in the sanctuary of the God of Israel.

verses.zh: 因此，耶和华的忿怒临到犹大和耶路撒冷，将其中的人抛来抛去，令人惊骇、嗤笑，正如你们亲眼所见的。
verses.en: The Lord was angry at Judah and Jerusalem and made them an appalling object of horror at which people hiss out their scorn,[NOTE:1] as you can see with your own eyes.
notes: Heb “and he made them [an object] of dread and devastation and hissing.”

verses.zh: 所以我们的祖宗倒在刀下，我们的妻子儿女也被掳掠。
verses.en: Look, our fathers died violently,[NOTE:1] and our sons, daughters, and wives were carried off[NOTE:2] because of this.

verses.zh: 现在我心中有意与耶和华―以色列的　神立约，好使他的烈怒转离我们。
verses.en: Now I intend[NOTE:1] to make a covenant with the Lord God of Israel, so that he may relent from his raging anger.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “now it is with my heart.”
Heb “so that the rage of his anger might turn from us.” The jussive with vav (ו) conjunctive indicates purpose/result after the preceding statement of intention.

verses.zh: 我的众子啊，现在不要懈怠；因为耶和华拣选你们站在他面前事奉他，与他烧香。」
verses.en: My sons, do not be negligent now, for the Lord has chosen you to stand in his presence, to minister to him,[NOTE:1] to be his ministers,[NOTE:2] and offer sacrifices.”[NOTE:3]
notes: That is, to conduct the religious rituals directed to the Lord.
That is, to be his ministers for the nation.

Heb “ones who cause [sacrifices] to go up in smoke.” The Hiphil form of קָטַר (qatar) can refer specifically to offering incense (e.g. 2 Chr 26:19; 32:12), but it may also be a general word for making sacrifices (e.g. 1 Chr 6:49). If it refers to burning incense, then the altar of incense in the Holy place of the tabernacle may be in view. Otherwise it is more general (they sacrifice animals later in this chapter, 2 Chr 29:21-24) and includes making sacrifices as well as offering incense.

verses.zh: 于是，利未人哥辖的子孙、亚玛赛的儿子玛哈，亚撒利雅的儿子约珥；米拉利的子孙、亚伯底的儿子基士，耶哈利勒的儿子亚撒利雅；革顺的子孙、薪玛的儿子约亚，约亚的儿子伊甸；
verses.en: The following Levites prepared to carry out the king’s orders:[NOTE:1] From the Kohathites: Mahath son of Amasai and Joel son of Azariah;from the Merarites: Kish son of Abdi and Azariah son of Jehallelel;from the Gershonites: Joah son of Zimmah and Eden son of Joah;

verses.zh: 以利撒反的子孙申利和耶利；亚萨的子孙撒迦利雅和玛探雅；
verses.en: from the descendants of Elizaphan: Shimri and Jeiel;from the descendants of Asaph: Zechariah and Mattaniah;

verses.zh: 希幔的子孙耶歇和示每；耶杜顿的子孙示玛雅和乌薛；
verses.en: from the descendants of Heman: Jehiel and Shimei;from the descendants of Jeduthun: Shemaiah and Uzziel.

verses.zh: 起来聚集他们的弟兄，洁净自己，照着王的吩咐、耶和华的命令，进去洁净耶和华的殿。
verses.en: They assembled their brothers and consecrated themselves. Then they went in to purify the Lord’s temple, just as the king had ordered, in accordance with the word[NOTE:1] of the Lord.

verses.zh: 祭司进入耶和华的殿要洁净殿，将殿中所有污秽之物搬到耶和华殿的院内，利未人接去，搬到外头汲沦溪边。
verses.en: The priests then entered the Lord’s temple to purify it; they brought out to the courtyard of the Lord’s temple every ceremonially unclean thing they discovered inside.[NOTE:1] The Levites took them out to the Kidron Valley.
notes: Heb “in the temple of the Lord.”

verses.zh: 从正月初一日洁净起，初八日到了耶和华的殿廊，用八日的工夫洁净耶和华的殿，到正月十六日才洁净完了。
verses.en: On the first day of the first month they began consecrating; by the eighth day of the month they reached the porch of the Lord’s temple.[NOTE:1] For eight more days they consecrated the Lord’s temple. On the sixteenth day of the first month they were finished.

verses.zh: 于是，他们晋见希西家王，说：「我们已将耶和华的全殿和燔祭坛，并坛的一切器皿、陈设饼的桌子，与桌子的一切器皿都洁净了；
verses.en: They went to King Hezekiah and said: “We have purified the entire temple of the Lord, including the altar of burnt sacrifice and all its equipment, and the table for the Bread of the Presence and all its equipment.

verses.zh: 并且亚哈斯王在位犯罪的时候所废弃的器皿，我们预备齐全，且洁净了，现今都在耶和华的坛前。」
verses.en: We have prepared and consecrated all the items that King Ahaz removed during his reign when he acted unfaithfully. They are in front of the altar of the Lord.”

verses.zh: 希西家王清早起来，聚集城里的首领都上耶和华的殿；
verses.en: Early the next morning King Hezekiah assembled the city officials and went up to the Lord’s temple.

verses.zh: 牵了七只公牛，七只公羊，七只羊羔，七只公山羊，要为国、为殿、为犹大人作赎罪祭。王吩咐亚伦的子孙众祭司，献在耶和华的坛上，
verses.en: They brought seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven goats as a sin offering for the kingdom, the sanctuary, and Judah.[NOTE:1] The king[NOTE:2] told the priests, the descendants of Aaron, to offer burnt sacrifices on the altar of the Lord.
notes: Perhaps these terms refer metonymically to the royal court, the priests and Levites, and the people, respectively.
Heb “he”; the referent (the king) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 就宰了公牛，祭司接血洒在坛上，宰了公羊，把血洒在坛上，又宰了羊羔，也把血洒在坛上；
verses.en: They slaughtered the bulls, and the priests took the blood and splashed it on the altar. Then they slaughtered the rams and splashed the blood on the altar; next they slaughtered the lambs and splashed the blood on the altar.

verses.zh: 把那作赎罪祭的公山羊牵到王和会众面前，他们就按手在其上。
verses.en: Finally they brought the goats for the sin offering before the king and the assembly, and they placed their hands on them.

verses.zh: 祭司宰了羊，将血献在坛上作赎罪祭，为以色列众人赎罪，因为王吩咐将燔祭和赎罪祭为以色列众人献上。
verses.en: Then the priests slaughtered them. They offered their blood as a sin offering on the altar to make atonement for all Israel because the king had decreed[NOTE:1] that the burnt sacrifice and sin offering were for all Israel.

verses.zh: 王又派利未人在耶和华殿中敲钹，鼓瑟，弹琴，乃照大卫和他先见迦得，并先知拿单所吩咐的，就是耶和华藉先知所吩咐的。
verses.en: Hezekiah[NOTE:1] stationed the Levites in the Lord’s temple with cymbals and stringed instruments just as David, Gad the king’s prophet,[NOTE:2] and Nathan the prophet had ordered. (The Lord had actually given these orders through his prophets.)
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Hezekiah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 利未人拿大卫的乐器，祭司拿号，一同站立。
verses.en: The Levites had[NOTE:1] David’s musical instruments and the priests had trumpets.

verses.zh: 希西家吩咐在坛上献燔祭，燔祭一献，就唱赞美耶和华的歌，用号，并用以色列王大卫的乐器相和。
verses.en: Hezekiah ordered the burnt sacrifice to be offered on the altar. As they began to offer the sacrifice, they also began to sing to the Lord, accompanied by the trumpets and the musical instruments of King David of Israel.

verses.zh: 会众都敬拜，歌唱的歌唱，吹号的吹号，如此直到燔祭献完了。
verses.en: The entire assembly worshiped, as the singers sang and the trumpeters played. They continued until the burnt sacrifice was completed.

verses.zh: 献完了祭，王和一切跟随的人都俯伏敬拜。
verses.en: When the sacrifices were completed, the king and all who were with him bowed down and worshiped.

verses.zh: 希西家王与众首领又吩咐利未人用大卫和先见亚萨的诗词颂赞耶和华；他们就欢欢喜喜地颂赞耶和华，低头敬拜。
verses.en: King Hezekiah and the officials told the Levites to praise the Lord, using the psalms[NOTE:1] of David and Asaph the prophet.[NOTE:2] So they joyfully offered praise and bowed down and worshiped.

verses.zh: 希西家说：「你们既然归耶和华为圣，就要前来把祭物和感谢祭奉到耶和华殿里。」会众就把祭物和感谢祭奉来，凡甘心乐意的也将燔祭奉来。
verses.en: Hezekiah said, “Now you have consecrated yourselves[NOTE:1] to the Lord. Come and bring sacrifices and thank offerings[NOTE:2] to the Lord’s temple.” So the assembly brought sacrifices and thank offerings, and whoever desired to do so[NOTE:3] brought burnt sacrifices.
notes: Heb “and all who were willing of heart.”

verses.zh: 会众所奉的燔祭如下：公牛七十只，公羊一百只，羊羔二百只，这都是作燔祭献给耶和华的；
verses.en: The assembly brought a total of 70 bulls, 100 rams, and 200 lambs as burnt sacrifices to the Lord,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and the number of burnt sacrifices which the assembly brought was seventy bulls, one hundred rams, two hundred lambs; for a burnt sacrifice to the Lord were all these.”

verses.zh: 又有分别为圣之物，公牛六百只，绵羊三千只。
verses.en: and 600 bulls and 3,000 sheep[NOTE:1] were consecrated.
notes: The Hebrew term צֹאן (tsoʾn) denotes smaller livestock in general; depending on context it can refer to sheep only or goats only, but there is nothing in the immediate context here to specify one or the other.

verses.zh: 但祭司太少，不能剥尽燔祭牲的皮，所以他们的弟兄利未人帮助他们，直等燔祭的事完了，又等别的祭司自洁了；因为利未人诚心自洁，胜过祭司。
verses.en: But there were not enough priests to skin all the animals,[NOTE:1] so their brothers, the Levites, helped them until the work was finished and the priests could consecrate themselves. (The Levites had been more conscientious about consecrating themselves than the priests.)[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “for the Levites were more pure of heart to consecrate themselves than the priests.”

verses.zh: 燔祭和平安祭牲的脂油，并燔祭同献的奠祭甚多。这样，耶和华殿中的事务俱都齐备了（或译：就整顿了）。
verses.en: There was a large number of burnt sacrifices, as well as fat from the peace offerings and drink offerings that accompanied the burnt sacrifices. So the service of the Lord’s temple was reinstituted.[NOTE:1]

verses.zh: 这事办的甚速，希西家和众民都喜乐，是因　神为众民所预备的。
verses.en: Hezekiah and all the people were happy about what God had done[NOTE:1] for them,[NOTE:2] for it had been done quickly.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “the people.” The pronoun “them” has been used here for stylistic reasons, to avoid redundancy.
